text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hariri said:" There will be no war in the region and no American move is expected before April".
-Lebanon decided to open an embassy in Armenia, Foreign Minister Bouez said.
-The Lebanese military prosecuter charged four Lebanese men with collaborating with Israel.
-Lebanon's Byblos Bank launched a $300-million EuroCD programme, chairman of the Bank Francois Bassil said.
-Foreign Minister Bouez said Israel's decision to build homes for Jews in Arab East Jeusalem threatens to wreck the peace process.
-Israeli forces shell inhabited areas in south Lebanon.

-Two Lebanese civilians were killed and three were wounded in Israeli shelling in south Lebanon in February. There were nine Israeli breaches of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding in south Lebanon that month.
-Prime Minister Hariri will decrease his stake in Solidere, Lebanon's biggest company, to $90 million from $125 million.
-Canada's Foreign Trade Minister met Hariri during a brief visit to Beirut on Thursday.
-President Hrawi demanded the Minister of Justice to clarify within 48 hours the issue of Japanese Red Army members reported arrested in Lebanon.
